cancellation.applicability: synchronous primitive; cancellation belongs to an outer caller

There is no lock acquisition timeout or explicit lock destruction; interruption/native worker behavior still requires #12553 observation.

timeout.applicability: no intrinsic filesystem/lock deadline in these helpers
timeout.expected: Do not infer a bounded native operation or released lock from an outer timeout. The collector serializes cache resets and reads under the reentrant lock. Normal and Python-exception exits release the acquisition through the with statement. There is no lock acquisition timeout or explicit lock destruction; interruption/native worker behavior still requires #12553 observation.
timeout.observation: Record the outer deadline and actual close/release completion independently.

retry.applicability: next collector call; no internal retry in these primitives
retry.expected: A new collector call resets text caches under the same retained lock. File/scanner allocations are per operation; this implies no transactional/idempotency guarantee.
retry.observation: Compare per-attempt handles and the process-scoped lock identity before/after retry.

normal.expected: The lexical context owns this acquisition after successful __enter__; its exit closes the acquired handle. Failed __enter__/descriptor-to-stream transfer is a separate error barrier. Synchronous pathlib operation owns its temporary file stream; inspect opening/closing and errors inside this library boundary, not a persistent store connection. Calling store delegates the transient handle to its concrete atomic/append helper; helper ownership is not a second store connection. Observe helper enter/transfer/exit.
normal.observation: At acquisition and owning return/exit: resource identity, open/close events, physical handles/threads/tasks remaining.

error.applicability: applicable after successful acquisition; no close obligation for a handle never created
error.expected: Preserve original failure while executing the documented cleanup boundary; record partial construction separately.
error.observation: Inject before allocation, after allocation, during use and during close; inspect actual cleanup and retained handles.

cancellation.applicability: owning async/thread boundary; primitive itself synchronous
cancellation.expected: Propagate cancellation after documented cleanup/drain; do not infer stopped native work from a cancelled future.
cancellation.observation: Cancel owner before/use/close barriers and observe physical completion, retained process-scope resources and caller outcome.

timeout.applicability: owning deadline; no intrinsic timeout claimed for synchronous primitive
timeout.expected: Apply the source-defined deadline; record any deliberately surviving process/global resources or blocking worker. Timeout is not a shutdown receipt.
timeout.observation: Observe deadline, close/drain completion and remaining resources separately. If no intrinsic deadline exists, inject at outer owner boundary.

retry.applicability: outer caller attempt; primitive does not imply an internal retry loop
retry.expected: Record retained owner versus fresh allocation and close failed-attempt resources; do not infer idempotent append/commit.
retry.observation: Barrier before retry; compare opened/closed/remaining IDs per attempt and shared owner lifetime.
